findings.title: align=False crashes with 'unknown model: False' although the docstring documents False as 'no alignment'
findings.description: analyze()'s align docstring says: 'If False or None, no alignment is applied (default: None).' Passing align=False raises ValueError on BOTH code paths (legacy and return_model=True/build_pipeline). tools/align.py only short-circuits align is None (and rejects align is True with a dedicated message); False falls through and is treated as a model name by the dispatcher (hypertools/align/align.py line ~324). Users toggling alignment programmatically (align=do_align and ...) hit this. Inconsistent with normalize=False, which is handled as skip on both paths.

findings.title: cluster= combined with a no-transform reducer (TSNE, MDS) crashes: AttributeError in the post-cluster data-recovery loop
findings.description: analyze() documents TSNE/MDS/SpectralEmbedding among supported reduce models and cluster= as composable with them. When cluster= is given, analyze re-applies the fitted non-cluster steps via _step_transform to recover the pre-cluster transformed data (analyze.py lines 169-183). For reducers with no out-of-sample .transform (sklearn TSNE, MDS), Reducer.transform calls model.transform and crashes with a raw AttributeError -- with OR without return_model. The pre-cluster data had already been computed inside pipe.fit_transform and was discarded. Same raw AttributeError surfaces when reusing a fitted pipeline containing such a reducer via pipeline= on new data (inherent TSNE limitation, but the error should be a friendly 'TSNE has no out-of-sample transform' message, not a leaked AttributeError).

findings.expected: Returns the TSNE-embedded (pre-cluster) data as documented; at minimum a clear error naming the limitation and a workaround.

findings.title: Unknown kwargs in the align dict spec are silently swallowed (HyperAlign.__init__ takes **kwargs)
findings.description: The docstring's own dict form align={'model': 'HyperAlign', 'kwargs': {...}} performs no kwarg validation: HyperAlign.__init__(self, n_iter=10, **kwargs) absorbs anything, so a typo (e.g. 'n_itr' for 'n_iter', or any bogus key) is accepted without error or warning on BOTH analyze code paths -- the user believes the parameter took effect. reduce= and cluster= dict specs correctly raise TypeError naming the unknown kwarg (e.g. "PCA.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'bogus_param'"). Per audit rule, silent acceptance of a wrong kwarg = major.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; d=[np.random.rand(30,6) for _ in range(2)]; out=hyp.analyze(d, align={'model':'HyperAlign','kwargs':{'bogus':5}}); print('silently accepted:', type(out)); out2=hyp.analyze(d, align={'model':'HyperAlign','kwargs':{'bogus':5}}, return_model=True); print('pipeline path too:', type(out2))"
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError naming the unknown HyperAlign kwarg, matching reduce=/cluster= behavior.
findings.actual:
silently accepted: <class 'list'>
pipeline path too: <class 'tuple'>
(HyperAlign.__init__ sig: (self, n_iter=10, **kwargs); HyperAlign(bogus=5) constructs fine and stores .bogus)
docs_impact: hypertools/tools/analyze.py (docstring example uses this dict form)

findings.title: Docstring claims ndims=/impute= are 'still honored' with pipeline=; both are silently ignored (only internal= is honored)
findings.description: analyze() pipeline= docstring: "`ndims=`/`internal=`/`impute=` are still honored (`internal=True` still guarantees a list is returned...)". The pipeline= branch (analyze.py lines 131-144) only implements internal=; ndims and impute never reach pipeline.transform. Verified: a pipeline fitted with ndims=3 still returns 3-dim output when called with ndims=2; NaN data transformed with impute='Kalman' is byte-identical to the default-PPCA call (impute ignored; the fitted normalize step's formatter always uses PPCA).
findings.repro:
PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng=np.random.default_rng(11); d=[rng.normal(size=(40,8)) for _ in range(3)]
nd=[x.copy() for x in d]
for x in nd: x.ravel()[rng.choice(x.size,10,replace=False)]=np.nan
res,f=hyp.analyze(d,normalize='across',reduce='PCA',ndims=3,return_model=True,random_state=0)
print('ndims=2 ->',[np.asarray(x).shape for x in hyp.analyze(d,pipeline=f,ndims=2)])
a=hyp.analyze(nd,pipeline=f,impute='Kalman'); b=hyp.analyze(nd,pipeline=f)
print('impute ignored:', all(np.allclose(np.asarray(x),np.asarray(y)) for x,y in zip(a,b)))"
findings.expected: Either honor ndims=/impute= on the pipeline= branch or document that only internal= applies.

findings.title: Docstring documents wrong defaults: reduce 'default: IncrementalPCA' and normalize 'across ... (default)' -- actual default for both is None (stage skipped)
findings.description: analyze()'s reduce docstring says "(default: 'IncrementalPCA')" and the normalize docstring says "If set to 'across', the columns ... will be z-scored across lists (default)". The signature defaults are reduce=None and normalize=None, which SKIP those stages entirely (verified: analyze(data) returns the input objects unchanged, identity). The wording was inherited from reduce()'s/normalize()'s own docstrings where those ARE the callable defaults; in analyze they are not.

findings.title: ndims= without reduce= is silently ignored (no warning) on both code paths
findings.description: analyze(data, ndims=3) returns the data UNREDUCED with no warning (legacy path: reduce=None short-circuits inside reduce(); pipeline path: build_pipeline omits the reduce stage entirely, returning Pipeline([])). Combined with F15-analyze-005's wrong documented default ('IncrementalPCA'), a scientist writing hyp.analyze(data, ndims=3) reasonably expects 3-D output and silently gets full-dimensional data. A warning ('ndims= given but reduce=None; no reduction performed') or defaulting reduce to IncrementalPCA when ndims is set would prevent silent wrong-shape results downstream.
